READ-ONLY research. WebSearch/WebFetch; cite with dates. Write to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\agents-improvements.md; return a concise summary. No installs, no MCP, no code changes.

Topic: concrete, evidence-based ways to make AI agents MORE POWERFUL / FASTER / SMARTER / MORE CREATIVE, each tagged with the strength of evidence and the honest risk it doesn't generalize. Cover: test-time compute / reasoning (and its cost tradeoff), better tool use + verification/self-consistency, memory + retrieval quality, multi-agent orchestration (when it actually helps vs adds cost), latency methods (speculative decoding, caching, smaller models for easy subtasks), fine-tuning/distillation of small specialist models, prompt/context engineering, and creativity methods (sampling/diversity like Verbalized Sampling) that don't hurt correctness. For each: expected effect, cost, and what a SMALL team could realistically implement as a product layer on top of frontier models (not training a frontier model). Distinguish proven from hyped.

handback.t:
Report written to C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\agents-improvements.md. It has one section per topic (effect, cost, small-team layer, evidence strength, why it may not generalize), a proven-vs-hyped table, an adoption order and a source list.

Sources are web-search summaries, not full-paper reads. I cross-checked nothing against the original papers. Several 2026 arXiv items I saw only as titles or snippets; I marked those "unverified" in the file. Most headline numbers are vendor-reported on internal evals or come from single preprints.

**Proven, adopt now:**
- **External verification:** tests, schemas or validators with retry-on-error work. Pure self-critique does not: "LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet" and 2026 follow-ups show accuracy loss without an outside signal.
- **Reliability metric:** measure agents with pass^k, not pass@1. tau-bench (Jun 2024): gpt-4o scored ~61% on retail at pass^1 and ~25% at pass^8.
- **Retrieval:** Anthropic Contextual Retrieval (Sept 2024) cut top-20 retrieval failures 35% with contextual embeddings, 49% adding contextual BM25, and 67% adding reranking (vendor-reported). Chroma's 2025 context-rot study found all 18 frontier models degrade as input grows, so prune and compact context.
- **Cost and latency:**
  - Prompt caching reportedly cuts latency 80-90% on long prefixes.
  - Model routing: RouteLLM (ICLR 2025) reports 85% cost reduction at 95% of GPT-4 quality on MT-Bench; FrugalGPT (2023) reports up to 98%.
  - Speculative decoding (1.5-3x throughput) is a serving-side technique, so a small team using hosted APIs mostly doesn't control it.
- **Reasoning budgets:** more thinking has sharply diminishing returns and can hurt ("When More Thinking Hurts", Apr 2026). Splitting a fixed token budget across parallel samples plus a vote beat one long chain by up to 22% at 16K tokens. Use adaptive effort per request.
- **Fine-tuning small specialists:** LoRA Land (310 fine-tuned 7B models) found they rival or beat GPT-4 on many narrow tasks. Only worth it for high-volume, stable, labelable tasks; the evidence says nothing about general agent capability.

**Moderate evidence:**
- **Multi-agent:** Anthropic's lead-plus-subagents research system beat single Opus 4 by 90.2% on their internal eval, at ~15x the tokens of chat. The Google/MIT study of 260 configurations (Dec 2025) found +81% on parallelizable tasks but 39-70% degradation on sequential ones. At matched compute, a single agent matches or beats multi-agent on multi-hop reasoning (Apr 2026). Use subagents only for parallel breadth work, context isolation or independent review.
- **Creativity:** Verbalized Sampling (Oct 2025) reports 1.6-2.1x more diversity and about 25.7% higher human-rated originality in creative writing, with no loss in factual accuracy in the authors' tests. Costs k times the generation, and small models estimate the probabilities poorly. I found no independent replication. Use it only in ideation steps, then select with a verifier.

**Hyped or weak:**
- many-role agent swarms and consensus voting for sequential work
- intrinsic self-reflection without feedback
- always-maximum thinking
- elaborate memory architectures without ablations
- magic prompt tricks, which vary by model version

**Suggested order for a small team:**
1. Build an eval harness with pass^k on your own tasks.
2. Add caching, context pruning and clean tool schemas.
3. Add external verification with retry-on-error.
4. Add hybrid retrieval with a reranker, and compaction or notes for memory.
5. Add routing and reasoning-effort control.
6. Use parallel subagents and diverge-then-converge ideation where the task fits.
7. Distill small specialists last, only for stable high-volume steps.
